question.text: An InvIT has a post-issue capital of Rs. 2,500 crore calculated at offer price. What is the minimum value of units that must be offered and allotted to the public?

explanation.text: The Logic: Since the post-issue capital (Rs. 2,500 crore) is at least Rs. 1,600 crore and less than Rs. 4,000 crore, the minimum offer to public shall be of the value of at least Rs. 400 crore as per InvIT Regulations. The Trap: 25% applies only when post-issue capital is less than Rs. 1,600 crore. 10% applies when post-issue capital is Rs. 4,000 crore or more. The Rs. 400 crore floor applies only in the middle tier. Note: The InvIT public-offer rule has three tiers: at least 25% of post-issue capital if it is less than Rs. 1,600 crore; at least Rs. 400 crore if it is at least Rs. 1,600 crore and less than Rs. 4,000 crore; and at least 10% if it is at least Rs. 4,000 crore.
